title: Serenade for Strings in E major
hook: Five sunny movements for strings alone, written in under two weeks during one of the happiest springs of Dvořák’s life.

painting.title: Lovers
painting.pairingNote: A young couple sits in the grass under spring leaves, painted in 1875, the year Dvořák, two years married, wrote his serenade; the painting now hangs in Prague.

facts: Dvořák wrote the Serenade in May 1875, between the 3rd and the 14th: about twelve days. He was thirty-three, two years married, and had just won an Austrian state grant for the first time.

A [[serenade|serenade]] was originally light evening music, often played outdoors. Dvořák’s is for string orchestra alone, in five short movements; all but the finale have a simple song-like shape with a contrasting middle.

It was first played in Prague on 10 December 1876, at the Žofín Palace, conducted by Adolf Čech. It was such a success that it was programmed again at once. Leoš Janáček conducted it in Brno the next spring, and in August 1877 it was the work with which Dvořák made his first documented appearance as a conductor.
At the end of the finale, the opening tune of the first movement comes back, so the whole work closes where it began.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a gentle song (I), a wistful waltz (II), a playful chase (III), a tender slow movement (IV), a lively village dance that looks back before it ends (V).

movements.heading: Moderato
movements.summary: A calm, singing opening. Over a steady pulse in the violas, the second violins and cellos share a warm melody, and the first violins soon float above it. A livelier middle section with a skipping rhythm briefly changes the mood before the song returns.

mainIdeas.name: The song
mainIdeas.description: a gentle, lyrical melody passed between second violins and cellos, in E major.

mainIdeas.name: The dance
mainIdeas.description: a bouncier tune in G major, built on a dotted, skipping rhythm.

stops.hear: The violas keep up a soft, even pulse; the second violins and cellos sing a warm melody
stops.happening: The main tune, in E major

stops.hear: The first violins rise above with a soaring line while the tune continues underneath
stops.happening: The melody grows into a duet

stops.hear: The music brightens and starts to skip, with dotted rhythms
stops.happening: The middle section, in G major

stops.hear: The calm opening melody returns

stops.label: Last 20 seconds
stops.hear: The music settles and ends on three soft chords
stops.happening: A quiet close in E major

notice: Listen for who has the tune at the start. It is not the first violins, as you might expect, but the second violins and cellos, in the middle of the sound.

movements.heading: Tempo di valse
movements.summary: A [[waltz|waltz]], but a gentle, slightly melancholy one, in C-sharp minor. The dance tune is followed by brighter episodes, and a contrasting middle section moves into a warm major key before the waltz returns. At the very end the minor turns to major.

mainIdeas.name: The waltz
mainIdeas.description: a lilting, wistful tune in C-sharp minor.

mainIdeas.name: The second tune
mainIdeas.description: a more flowing melody in a major key.

mainIdeas.name: The middle section
mainIdeas.description: a smoother, more continuous dance in D-flat major.

stops.hear: A swaying, wistful dance tune in the violins
The tune is heard again, then the music turns brighter
stops.happening: The first part repeated, then a major-key phrase

stops.hear: A new, more flowing melody
The waltz tune returns and ends with a loud minor chord
stops.happening: The end of the first section

stops.hear: A smoother, warmer dance, with lines answering each other
stops.happening: The middle section, the [[trio|trio]], in D-flat major

stops.hear: The wistful waltz returns

stops.label: Last 15 seconds
stops.hear: The final chord comes out in the major

notice: Listen to the very last chord. After a whole movement in the minor, it ends in the major, a small surprise.

movements.heading: Scherzo: Vivace
movements.summary: A quick, playful [[scherzo|scherzo]] in F major. Its main tune is a [[canon|canon]]: one group of strings starts it, and another follows close behind with the same notes, as if chasing it. A broader, singing section gives a moment of calm, but the chase keeps coming back.

mainIdeas.name: The chase
mainIdeas.description: a bright, bouncing tune that one group plays and another imitates a moment later.

mainIdeas.name: The song
mainIdeas.description: a broad, lyrical melody in a contrasting middle section.

stops.hear: A bouncy tune in one group of strings, followed at once by another group playing the same thing
The full string orchestra, louder, with the tune tossed around
Slower and more singing: a broad melody in a new key
The bouncing chase returns
The tunes come together and the music presses towards the end

stops.label: Last 15 seconds
stops.hear: Bright, firm closing chords

notice: Try to follow the two groups in the opening chase. The second group always enters just after the first, like an echo that will not stop.

movements.heading: Larghetto
movements.summary: The quiet heart of the Serenade: a slow, tender song in A major. It begins very softly, grows warmer, passes through a more restless middle section and returns to its first calm.

mainIdeas.name: The melody
mainIdeas.description: a long, gentle line in the violins over soft chords in the lower strings.

mainIdeas.name: The middle
mainIdeas.description: more searching, with short phrases answering each other.

stops.hear: Very soft: a slow melody in the violins over quiet, held chords
stops.happening: The main melody, in A major

stops.hear: The melody rises and the sound grows fuller and warmer
Shorter phrases, more restless, passed between the instruments
The opening melody returns, as calm as before

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The music grows quieter and fades away

notice: Remember this melody. It comes back, briefly and wistfully, in the middle of the finale.

movements.heading: Finale: Allegro vivace
movements.summary: A lively finale with the energy of a Bohemian village dance, full of accents on the “wrong” beats. It brings three tunes, recalls the Larghetto, then the opening song of the first movement, and ends with a quick dash to three firm E major chords.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a lively, dotted tune after a short opening of falling figures.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a tune passed between violins and cellos over running notes in the violas.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 3
mainIdeas.description: a busy, energetic tune, with violins and cellos imitating each other.

stops.hear: Falling figures in imitation, then a lively, accented dance tune
Violins and cellos call and answer over busy violas
Fast, bustling notes and a new, energetic tune tossed between high and low
Suddenly slower and softer: the tender melody of the Larghetto returns
stops.happening: A memory of the slow movement

stops.hear: The dance starts again from the beginning
The music calms and the gentle song from the very start of the Serenade returns

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: A sudden burst of speed and three loud E major chords

notice: Listen for the two memories: first the Larghetto, then the opening song. Dvořák ties the five movements together, in what is called [[cyclic-form|cyclic form]].

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Marriner and the Academy recorded the Serenade in May 1970 in London’s Kingsway Hall, and the first LP paired it with Grieg’s Holberg Suite.

threads.title: A happy spring
threads.body: A state grant, a young marriage and a growing reputation: the Serenade has hardly a dark moment, and even its minor-key waltz ends in the major.

threads.title: Song and dance
threads.body: Every movement except the Larghetto dances: a gentle song with a skipping middle, a waltz, a chase, a village dance.

threads.title: Coming full circle
threads.body: The finale recalls the slow movement and then the opening tune, so the work ends where it began.

recordings.orchestra: Academy of St Martin in the Fields
